FlashAttention for Scalable Vector Architectures
papers.abstract_excerpt: Inference with transformer models on CPUs is increasingly important, especially for Small Language Models (SLMs), where vector architectures are emerging as a promising execution substrate. The attention module is a major bottleneck due to high memory bandwidth requirements; FlashAttention mitigates this by fusing operations to improve data locality and reduce intermediate memory traffic. papers.abstract_excerpt: FlashAttention computes attention one block of keys at a time and divides by the softmax normalizer only at the end. How large is its rounding error, and is it worse than that of ordinary two-pass attention? This note bounds the forward error of FlashAttention-2 for one query, compares it with two-pass attention, and measures the one place where it really goes wrong: the split-KV (Flash-Decoding) merge. papers.title: A FlashAttention-2-Enhanced Swin Masked Autoencoder Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Classification and Severity Grading
FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
papers.abstract_excerpt: Scaling Transformers to longer sequence lengths has been a major problem in the last several years, promising to improve performance in language modeling and high-resolution image understanding, as well as to unlock new applications in code, audio, and video generation. The attention layer is the main bottleneck in scaling to longer sequences, as its runtime and memory increase quadratically in the sequence length. FlashAttention exploits the asymmetric GPU memory hierarchy to bring significant memory saving (linear instead of quadratic) and runtime speedup (2-4$\times$ compared to optimized baselines), with no approximation.
